subtopic: Direct & Indirect Instruction, Inquiry, Cooperative Learning, & Questioning Techniques

items.definition: A teacher-directed instructional approach characterized by explicit teaching of concepts, step-by-step lecture, structured demonstration, guided practice, and immediate corrective feedback.
items.rationalization: Best used when teaching foundational skills, basic math algorithms, grammar rules, laboratory safety procedures, or step-by-step motor skills.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Distinguish direct vs indirect instructional strategies

items.definition: A student-centered instructional approach where the teacher acts as a facilitator, guiding students through active observation, inquiry, hypothesizing, problem-solving, and concept formation.
items.rationalization: Fosters higher-order critical thinking, self-regulation, curiosity, and deep conceptual understanding rather than rote recall.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Distinguish direct vs indirect instructional strategies

items.definition: A top-down instructional method that begins with the teacher stating a general rule, principle, or formula, followed by illustrative examples and student practice.
items.rationalization: Efficient and time-saving; moves from General to Specific (G to S). E.g., presenting the formula Area = L x W first, then having students solve sample rectangles.

mnemonic.title: Deductive Strategy
mnemonic.phrase: Deductive: Down from General to Specific

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Differentiate deductive and inductive instructional models

items.definition: A bottom-up instructional method that begins by presenting multiple concrete examples and observations, guiding students to discover patterns and formulate the general rule.
items.rationalization: Promotes active thinking and retention; moves from Specific to General (S to G). Also known as the discovery approach.

mnemonic.title: Inductive Strategy
mnemonic.phrase: Inductive: Increases from Specific to General

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Differentiate deductive and inductive instructional models

items.definition: An inquiry-based constructivist teaching sequence consisting of 5 phases: Engage (hook interest), Explore (hands-on investigation), Explain (clarify concepts), Elaborate (apply in new contexts), and Evaluate (assess mastery).
items.rationalization: Extensively recommended in Science and Mathematics teaching to allow learners to build conceptual models before formal definitions are introduced.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply the 5E inquiry cycle in lesson design

items.definition: An experiential DepEd lesson planning model consisting of Activity (concrete experience), Analysis (processing reflections and questions), Abstraction (generalizing key concepts), and Application (transfer to authentic life).
items.rationalization: Aligns with David Kolb's experiential learning theory, moving learners from concrete engagement through reflection to conceptual theory and practical usage.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Design lessons using the 4As constructivist model

items.definition: A structured instructional progression moving from high teacher support to independent learner competence: 'I Do' (teacher modeling), 'We Do' (guided practice), 'You Do Together' (collaborative work), and 'You Do Alone' (independent application).
items.rationalization: Developed by Pearson and Gallagher; prevents premature student failure by ensuring sufficient scaffolding before independent task execution.

mnemonic.title: Gradual Release
mnemonic.phrase: I Do, We Do, You Do Together, You Do Alone

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Sequence instructional scaffolding via Gradual Release of Responsibility

items.definition: A student-centered pedagogical strategy where learning is organized around solving an ill-structured, open-ended, real-world authentic problem with multiple possible solutions.
items.rationalization: Students work in teams to define the problem, identify what they need to know, research independently, and present justified solutions.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Implement Problem-Based and Project-Based learning

items.definition: An instructional approach where students engage in sustained inquiry over an extended period to investigate and respond to an authentic, engaging question, culminating in a tangible product or public presentation.
items.rationalization: Unlike problem-based learning which ends with a proposed solution, project-based learning always requires constructing a tangible artifact, model, or exhibition.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Implement Problem-Based and Project-Based learning

items.definition: A cooperative learning structure by Elliot Aronson where students are assigned to 'home groups' and 'expert groups'; each expert masters a specific segment of material and returns to teach it to their home group.
items.rationalization: Ensures positive interdependence and individual accountability because every member holds a vital piece of the learning puzzle.

mnemonic.title: Jigsaw Strategy
mnemonic.phrase: Pieces Fit Together in Jigsaw Groups

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply cooperative learning structures (Jigsaw, STAD, T-P-S)

items.definition: A three-step cooperative discussion strategy where students first reflect silently on a prompt (Think), discuss their thoughts with a peer (Pair), and share their insights with the whole class (Share).
items.rationalization: Increases student wait time, eliminates fear of public failure, and guarantees 100% active participation compared to traditional call-and-response questioning.

mnemonic.title: Think-Pair-Share
mnemonic.phrase: Think Alone, Pair with Pal, Share with School

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply cooperative learning structures (Jigsaw, STAD, T-P-S)

items.definition: A cooperative learning model where heterogeneous teams of 4-5 students study together after teacher presentation, take individual quizzes, and earn team rewards based on individual improvement scores.
items.rationalization: Fairly recognizes and rewards lower-performing students because team points derive from surpassing one's own baseline score rather than absolute rank.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply cooperative learning structures (Jigsaw, STAD, T-P-S)

items.definition: A dynamic discussion technique where an inner circle of students discusses a controversial topic while an outer circle of students silently observes, takes notes, and later swaps seats.
items.rationalization: Develops active listening, turn-taking, argumentation analysis, and constructive peer evaluation.

mnemonic.title: Fishbowl Discussion
mnemonic.phrase: Inner Swimmers Speak, Outer Observers Seek

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Utilize classroom discussion and dialogue formats

items.definition: A disciplined, probing questioning dialogue that challenges assumptions, clarifies definitions, examines evidence, explores consequences, and stimulates critical thinking.
items.rationalization: Uses open-ended questions to guide students in recognizing contradictions in their reasoning and discovering truth autonomously.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Demonstrate effective questioning and prompting techniques

items.definition: The deliberate pedagogical pause of at least 3 to 5 seconds observed by the teacher after asking a question (Wait Time 1) and after a student responds (Wait Time 2).
items.rationalization: Significantly increases response length, participation of slower learners, higher-order thinking, and spontaneous student-to-student interactions.

mnemonic.title: Wait Time
mnemonic.phrase: Three Seconds Pause Prompts Profound Thinking

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Demonstrate effective questioning and prompting techniques

items.definition: Convergent questions require a single, predetermined, correct factual answer (low cognitive level), whereas Divergent questions invite multiple valid perspectives, creative solutions, and open-ended exploration (high cognitive level).
items.rationalization: Effective teachers balance convergent recall questions during review with divergent analytical questions during concept development.

mnemonic.title: Questioning Types
mnemonic.phrase: Convergent Closes to One, Divergent Drives Many

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Demonstrate effective questioning and prompting techniques

items.definition: A teacher's constant perceptual awareness of everything transpiring in all corners of the classroom at all times ('having eyes in the back of one's head').
items.rationalization: Allows the teacher to nip misbehavior in the bud before it escalates, demonstrating prompt and targeted intervention to the correct perpetrator.

mnemonic.title: Withitness
mnemonic.phrase: With It: Knowing All What's Going On
items: E - Eyes in the back of head

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: The teacher's supervisory ability to attend to two or more separate classroom events, tasks, or student needs simultaneously without losing momentum.
items.rationalization: E.g., helping a small reading group while quietly walking over to hand a pencil to an off-task student without interrupting the group lesson.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: Smoothness is maintaining lesson flow without sudden teacher digressions or erratic jumps; Momentum is maintaining steady pacing without unnecessary pauses or dragging slowdowns.
items.rationalization: Prevents behavioral flare-ups; lesson breakdowns occur when teachers get sidetracked by trivial matters (dangle, flip-flop, thrust).
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: A pedagogical error where the teacher terminates an activity, initiates a new topic, and then abruptly returns to the previous topic, confusing the learners.
items.rationalization: Disrupts students' mental frame and derails lesson continuity.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: Leaving an instructional thought, explanation, or sentence hanging in mid-air because the teacher gets distracted by something else in the room.
items.rationalization: Leaves learners suspended without conceptual closure.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: Bursting into a student activity with sudden announcements or instructions when students are deeply engrossed, breaking their concentration.
items.rationalization: Teachers should wait for a natural lull or establish a gentle cue before interjecting new instructions.

mnemonic.title: Thrust
mnemonic.phrase: Thrusting In Uninvited While Students Work

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: Spending excessive, unnecessary time preaching about misbehavior or repeating explanations long after students have already understood.
items.rationalization: Bores students, kills lesson momentum, and invites secondary behavioral disruptions.

mnemonic.title: Overdwelling
mnemonic.phrase: Dwelling Too Long On Dull Details

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: The phenomenon where correcting the misbehavior of one student in a clear, firm, and calm manner influences and improves the behavior of other observing students.
items.rationalization: Works best when the correction specifies the unacceptable behavior and names the alternative desired conduct without personal anger.

mnemonic.title: Ripple Effect
mnemonic.phrase: Calm Correction Waves Across the Classroom

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply Jacob Kounin's classroom management principles

items.definition: A proactive instructional philosophy that tailors Content (what students learn), Process (how they make sense), Product (how they show mastery), and Learning Environment to students' readiness, interest, and profile.
items.rationalization: Rejects one-size-fits-all teaching; uses tiered activities, flexible grouping, and varied modalities to ensure all learners are challenged appropriately.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Differentiate instruction for diverse learning profiles

items.definition: A differentiation technique where students work on the same essential concept or standard, but the complexity of tasks, reading levels, or support varies across ability tiers.
items.rationalization: Ensures equity and challenge; struggling learners receive scaffolded tasks while advanced learners work on higher-order abstract applications.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Differentiate instruction for diverse learning profiles

items.definition: Temporary instructional support structures provided by the teacher or peer to help the learner perform a task within their Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD), gradually removed as autonomy increases.
items.rationalization: Examples include graphic organizers, sentence stems, teacher modeling, checklist rubrics, and think-aloud protocols.

mnemonic.title: Scaffolding
mnemonic.phrase: Support While Building, Removed When Strong

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply scaffolding within the Zone of Proximal Development

items.definition: An instructional reading strategy where teachers and students take turns leading structured dialogue using four comprehension strategies: Predicting, Questioning, Clarifying, and Summarizing (PQCS).
items.rationalization: Dramatically boosts reading comprehension by scaffolding metacognitive monitoring and shifting students from passive readers to active meaning-makers.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Implement Reciprocal Teaching for reading comprehension

items.definition: A three-column metacognitive graphic organizer tracking what students already Know (K), what they Want to know (W), and what they have Learned (L).
items.rationalization: Activates prior schema, establishes personal inquiry goals, and provides reflective closure for new concepts.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Select graphic organizers for cognitive processing

items.definition: A visual organizer using overlapping circles to highlight similarities and differences between two or more concepts, characters, or phenomena.
items.rationalization: Enhances comparative analysis and higher-order analytical evaluation.

mnemonic.title: Venn Diagram
mnemonic.phrase: Overlapping Circles of Compare and Contrast

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Select graphic organizers for cognitive processing

items.definition: A blended pedagogical strategy where direct instruction/lecture is moved outside the classroom via pre-recorded videos or readings, dedicating precious classroom time to active collaborative problem-solving, debates, and hands-on projects.
items.rationalization: Flips Bloom's taxonomy: lower-order remembering occurs at home at student's own pace; higher-order analyzing and creating occurs in class with teacher guidance.

mnemonic.title: Flipped Classroom
mnemonic.phrase: Lecture at Home, Homework in Class

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply modern blended and flipped teaching models

items.definition: An instructional technique where the teacher performs a process, shows an experiment, or models a skill while explaining each step, followed by student imitation (return demonstration).
items.rationalization: Essential in TVL courses, science laboratory setups, and psychomotor skills to ensure safety, precision, and error correction.

mnemonic.title: Demonstration Method
mnemonic.phrase: Show and Tell Followed by Student Return Demo

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Design demonstration and psychomotor skill lessons

items.term: Herbartian Steps of Teaching (Johann Friedrich Herbart)
items.definition: The classical formal instructional sequence: 1. Preparation, 2. Presentation, 3. Association / Comparison, 4. Generalization, and 5. Application.
items.rationalization: The historical ancestor of contemporary lesson plan structures, organizing instruction into a systematic pedagogical sequence.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Trace historical lesson planning models (Herbartian, Madeline Hunter)

items.definition: A 7-step direct instruction lesson model: Anticipatory Set, Objective and Purpose, Input, Modeling, Checking for Understanding, Guided Practice, and Independent Practice.
items.rationalization: Widely used in structured classroom teaching to guarantee that students do not practice errors during homework.

mnemonic.title: Madeline Hunter Model
mnemonic.phrase: Hook, Teach, Model, Check, Guide, Independent

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Trace historical lesson planning models (Herbartian, Madeline Hunter)

items.term: DepEd Order No. 42, s. 2016 (Policy Guidelines on Daily Lesson Preparation)
items.definition: The DepEd policy standardizing lesson preparation: Newly-hired teachers prepare Detailed Lesson Plans (DLPs) for at least 1 year, while experienced teachers prepare Daily Lesson Logs (DLLs).
items.rationalization: Ensures teachers systematically plan instructional flow, align with curriculum guides, and integrate formative assessment.

mnemonic.title: DO 42 s. 2016
mnemonic.phrase: Detailed Lesson Plan vs Daily Lesson Log Guidelines
items: DLP - For new teachers (1 year min)

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd guidelines on lesson planning (DLP/DLL)

items.term: Detailed Lesson Plan (DLP) vs Daily Lesson Log (DLL)
items.definition: A DLP contains comprehensive verbatim teacher and student activities, questions, and responses across all lesson stages; a DLL is a concise template covering Objectives, Content, Learning Resources, Procedures, and Remarks.
items.rationalization: DLL reduces clerical burden on master teachers while retaining systematic tracking of competencies.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd guidelines on lesson planning (DLP/DLL)

items.definition: Instructional experiential strategies that place students in simulated real-life roles, scenarios, or simulations (e.g., mock court trial, UN assembly, emergency evacuation).
items.rationalization: Enhances empathy, problem-solving, communication skills, and affective perspective-taking in safe controlled settings.

mnemonic.title: Simulation & Role Play
mnemonic.phrase: Stepping into Shoes in Safe Scenarios

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Implement simulation and role-playing strategies

items.definition: An instructional technique using real-life descriptive narratives of complex dilemma situations, requiring students to diagnose issues, evaluate alternatives, and recommend ethical decisions.
items.rationalization: Popularized by Harvard Business and Law schools; highly effective for ethics, educational leadership, and civic decision-making.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Implement case study analysis in teaching

items.definition: A questioning follow-up technique that pushes students beyond superficial or initial answers to justify, clarify, elaborate, or provide concrete evidence.
items.rationalization: E.g., 'What evidence made you conclude that?' or 'Can you explain the reasoning behind your step?'
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Demonstrate effective questioning and prompting techniques

items.definition: Providing subtle verbal hints, leading clues, or simplified rephrasing when a student is stuck or hesitant, helping them successfully formulate the correct response.
items.rationalization: Prevents learner embarrassment, sustains confidence, and models problem-solving through guided scaffolding.

mnemonic.title: Prompting Clues
mnemonic.phrase: Providing Prompts to Prevent Paralyzing Hesitation

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Demonstrate effective questioning and prompting techniques

items.definition: Asking another student or the whole class to react to, elaborate upon, evaluate, or answer a question initially answered by a peer.
items.rationalization: Transforms teacher-centric dialogue into dynamic student-to-student discourse: 'Sarah, what do you think of Mark's solution?'

mnemonic.title: Redirecting Technique
mnemonic.phrase: Redirecting the Ball Across the Court

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Demonstrate effective questioning and prompting techniques

items.definition: A proactive school-wide framework that clearly teaches, models, and reinforces positive behavioral expectations rather than merely punishing misbehaviors.
items.rationalization: Research proves that reinforcing desirable conduct produces longer-lasting behavioral improvements and creates a supportive classroom climate.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply classroom management models (PBIS, Assertive Discipline)

items.definition: A classroom management approach emphasizing that teachers have the right to teach and students have the right to learn; the teacher establishes firm, clear rules and a transparent hierarchy of predictable consequences.
items.rationalization: Contrasts with passive (wishy-washy) or hostile (aggressive) teaching; assertive teachers are calm, firm, consistent, and supportive.

mnemonic.title: Assertive Discipline
mnemonic.phrase: Canters: Clear, Calm, and Consistent Consequences

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply classroom management models (PBIS, Assertive Discipline)

items.definition: Disciplinary consequences that are logically, naturally, and directly related to the misbehavior (unlike arbitrary punishment), helping students learn responsibility.
items.rationalization: E.g., if a student spills paint on the desk, the logical consequence is cleaning it up, not writing 100 sentences or sitting in the corner.

mnemonic.title: Logical Consequences
mnemonic.phrase: Dreikurs: Consequences Directly Connect to the Crime

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply classroom management models (PBIS, Assertive Discipline)

items.term: Dreikurs' Four Mistaken Goals of Misbehavior
items.definition: The four underlying psychological goals motivating student misbehavior: Attention-seeking, Power and control, Revenge, and Display of inadequacy (assumed disability).
items.rationalization: Teachers identify the goal by examining their own emotional reaction: Feeling annoyed = Attention; Feeling challenged/angry = Power; Feeling hurt = Revenge; Feeling helpless = Inadequacy.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Diagnose mistaken goals of student misbehavior

items.definition: An instructional arrangement where students act as tutors and tutees to help one another learn content, reinforcing knowledge for both participants (Docendo discimus).
items.rationalization: Cross-age or same-age tutoring builds social confidence; the tutor consolidates mastery while the tutee receives personalized pacing.

mnemonic.title: Peer Tutoring
items: D - Docendo discimus (by teaching we learn)

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Implement peer-mediated instructional strategies

items.definition: A blended classroom rotation model where students rotate on a set schedule through different learning stations, including at least one online learning station, one teacher-led small group station, and one collaborative station.
items.rationalization: Allows the teacher to conduct high-impact small group differentiated instruction while remaining students work independently or in pairs.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply modern blended and flipped teaching models

items.definition: The optimal authoritative classroom climate characterized by high warmth (care, empathy, emotional support) combined with high demandingness (high academic and behavioral expectations).
items.rationalization: Baumrind's authoritative style promotes high achievement and self-efficacy; indulgent (warm but low demands) or authoritarian (cold and harsh) styles harm growth.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Establish positive, supportive classroom learning environments

items.definition: A teaching technique where the teacher verbalizes their internal problem-solving and thinking processes aloud while tackling a difficult text, problem, or decision.
items.rationalization: Demystifies how expert minds think, enabling novices to observe internal strategies like monitoring, pausing, re-reading, and self-correcting.

mnemonic.title: Think-Aloud Protocol
mnemonic.phrase: Speaking Thoughts Aloud to Show the Brain at Work

items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Model metacognitive and self-regulation strategies

items.definition: Managing student attention and minor off-task behaviors using eye contact, physical proximity, subtle hand gestures, pausing, and facial expressions without interrupting verbal instruction.
items.rationalization: Preserves lesson momentum, avoids public confrontation, and saves vocal energy.
items.source: PRC BLEPT ProfEd Teaching Strategies Reviewer
items.tosCompetency: Apply nonverbal classroom management interventions
